prediction.likelyOutcome: Architectural Stainless has a genuine, trial-worthy claim on the agency/ownership theory given the court's own reconsideration ruling, but faces two independent, potentially dispositive threats — the belatedly-raised sworn-statement defense and the fact that the equipment was entirely removed from the premises before trial — either of which could defeat the foreclosure claim regardless of how agency is resolved. Net expected recovery is meaningfully discounted from the full $213,389.20 lien amount plaintiff has requested, with a real (not trivial) chance of a complete defense verdict.

issues.label: Failure to Provide CLA Sworn Statement (Statutory Prerequisite Defense)

outcome.description: After a bench trial the court held the construction lien attached only to the tenant's terminated leasehold interest, not the mall owner's real property (the lease permitted but did not require the improvements), found no cause of action and entered judgment for the mall owner against the $213,389.20 lien claim. The Court of Appeals affirmed.
outcome.finalNote: No-cause judgment for the owner affirmed.
